The driver runs against the `dispatch:local` server of this document's preamble, because it seeds every issue it reads at this head. `e2e/acceptance/tree-read-views.sh` is new here. It makes every read of the tree through `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree`.

The driver seeds, writing as `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN` where a person writes, one issue holding a comment thread a person wrote, a criterion under it, a requirement under that criterion, a decision an agent recorded with its `shaped` tuple to the requirement and a reading under that decision, a constraint the requirement's `constrained_by` names, a check that serves the requirement with one result, a plan task that serves it, an ask with its answer, and a person's approval of the verification query. It seeds a child issue holding a plan task and a check that serve the parent's requirement, the check with one result. Both hang from the child issue, because they serve no requirement of their own issue.

It reads `converted: true` for the seeded issue, which was born converted. Its `?view=spec` answers, as context, the decision whose `shaped` tuple names the requirement and the constraint the requirement's `constrained_by` names. The driver also writes, through dispatch://INFRA-1950's write routes, a lens of kind `pre-mortem` on the requirement with its `has_kind` tuple. The tree read with no view answers that lens as the tree's node, and, marked as context, the `pre-mortem` `lens_kind` node and the constraint, each with its `has_kind` or `constrained_by` tuple; it answers no other `lens_kind` or `constraint` node of the catalogue. The requirement's constraint is not the `pre-mortem` kind's source constraint, and the driver reads that source constraint absent, because a context node brings in no further context; it also seeds a second constraint that nothing names and reads it absent. It then retracts that `shaped` tuple and reads `?view=spec&v=` at the earlier version. That answer still holds the tie, while the current answer does not, and a version the query does not have answers 404. On the seeded issue, which holds a child, `?view=plan` answers the child's plan task with the parent's own, in one order, each marked with its issue. Its `?view=verification` answers, through `serves`, the child's check that serves the parent's requirement, with its result, marked with the child, and with the child issue as the check's parent. The parent's coverage reads that requirement as covered. The parent's tree read with no view answers the child's plan task through its `serves` tuple to the parent's requirement, marked with the child, and with the child issue as its parent. The driver gives that child plan task the block id of one of the parent's own plan tasks, and a `needs` tuple of its own; the read answers the two plan tasks with different `id`s and the same `block_id`, and each `serves` and `needs` tuple names its ends by those `id`s, so the driver tells the child's tuples from the parent's. Each view answers exactly its fixed kinds and context, and each node carries its parent's id, supertag and first line. Every node of the read with no view carries `visibility` and `made_at`: the comment thread reads `project` and the time the driver wrote it, within one second, and the lens reads the visibility the driver wrote it with. Each node also carries `text_tree`, and for the requirement, the comment that heads the thread and the decision it equals byte for byte the display tree that kind's own read answers (`GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug}/blocks`, the comment read and the decisions read). The driver then seeds a second issue it does not convert, whose spec holds a requirement it sets `proposed` and whose Verification document holds a check it sets `overtaken`, through dispatch://INFRA-1950's `/state` route. The driver also writes, as alice, a comment anchored inside the paragraph of the decision, by its quote and the decision's `block_id`, after it has written the same quote once more in a block above the decision, so only the block names the place, and then two more comments on the issue, writing again until the later one's id sorts below the earlier one's. The read with no view answers the anchored comment with the decision as its `parent`, answers the two comments after the issue's ranked children in the order they were written, and answers the decision with its review state, as `?view=decisions` does. The driver then keeps the decision as alice through the Keep route with the `text_sha256` that read answered, and the next read answers it `kept` by alice. That read with no view answers on the decision node every member `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` answers for it, each equal: `changed_at`, `kept` with `kept_by` and `kept_at`, `links` with each link's `stale`, and the rest of `model.Decision`; it answers the decision's `decided_by` tuple with its person as context. On the first issue's check that serves the requirement, it records a result, reads on the result node `verdict`, `retracted` null and `check_sha256` equal to the check node's `text_sha256`, then changes the check's words and reads the check's `text_sha256` and `changed_version` move while the result's `check_sha256` stays; it retracts the result and reads `retracted` with the reason. The driver then changes the words of the requirement that decision's `shaped` tuple names, and the next read answers that link `stale` true on the decision. It writes an ask in the spec, answers it as alice, and gives it a `shaped` tuple to the requirement, and `?view=spec` answers that ask as context with the tuple. On the converted issue it writes a comment whose anchor names the converted spec's artifact id, a quote and its `block_id`, and the comment is written and hangs under that block. As alice it then writes a comment on the issue under a command-bar run's header, through dispatch://INFRA-1950's run route. Alice's read with no view answers that run's `interaction` node as context with the comment's `changed_by_run` tuple to it, and the issue node holds no `changed_by_run` tuple of its own for that run. Bob's read answers the comment and neither the tuple nor the interaction. A further comment whose anchor names the decision's `block_id` with a quote that block does not hold is refused `400 INVALID_ANCHOR` naming `block_id`, and the issue holds no such comment. That issue's tree read answers `converted` false and `tree` null, while the first issue's answers `converted` true and a `tree` equal to the `room` the artifact read answers for each of its documents. The first issue's `view_of` is null. The driver seeds a converted child of the first issue that holds no requirement of its own, reads its `view_of` naming the first issue, and reads a requirement write on it refused `409 REQUIREMENT_BELONGS_TO_ANCESTOR` naming that same issue. It reads `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{tree}` and its `/text` answering 200 for the first issue's tree artifact, the text holding the criterion the driver wrote into the issue, and the issue read's documents list not naming the tree artifact. That issue's tree read with no view answers each of the two block nodes exactly once, under the parent R1 gives it, with the state it was set to, its `visibility`, `made_at` and `text_tree`, and a `document` member naming its document's artifact id and slug with the position the blocks read gives it. Last, the driver signs in as alice and writes an author-only lens on the first issue's requirement and a `project` risk under that lens. Read as alice, the risk's `parent` is the lens. The driver signs bob in through `GET /auth/_dev/signin?login=bob`, which the harness's reset seeds as it seeds alice (the root's `c-visibility` signs both in the same way). Read as bob, the no-view read answers the risk with the requirement as its `parent`, after the requirement's own children, no node, `parent` or tuple in that answer names the hidden lens's id, so neither its `has_kind` nor its `part_of` tuple appears, and its verdict and its findings' text appear nowhere in it. The hidden lens is a `pre-mortem` lens, because the risk route places a risk only under one, so the `pre-mortem` `lens_kind` is in bob's answer once, as the context of the visible lens. `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` still answers through this release. It answers the same decision nodes, each with the same review state, as `?view=decisions` of the tree read, because both read one query. The script then searches `packages/dispatch/web/src`, `packages/envoy-client/src` and `packages/daemon` for a caller of that route and finds none, after it finds a planted caller in a scratch copy of one file, so a search that matched nothing cannot read as a clean tree. The tree read's one answer carries the `serves`, `shaped`, `needs` and `constrained_by` tuples among the nodes it returns, and `?view=plan` carries each plan node's position, needs and size. `?view=verification` answers each check and result marked as the query's and each requirement above them marked as context, and the digest the approval records walks the query's nodes alone: a change to a context requirement's words leaves that digest unchanged. A second result recorded on the child's check leaves that digest unchanged too, because the parent's record holds no node of the child.

It gives the seeded child issue a design block. On the child issue, `?view=spec` answers the child's design blocks and the ancestor's requirements its checks serve, marked as context.

It then reads the spec, verification, plan and decisions views, which are filters of that one graph rather than trees of their own, and asserts each answers its own kinds out of it: the spec view the memo callout first where the issue has one, then the criterion and requirement nodes, the verification view the check and result nodes with each requirement they serve as context, the plan view the plan tasks, and the decisions view the asks with their answers, the decisions and the reading under an agent's decision. It asserts that a node reaches a view only through the graph, so no view answers a node the graph does not, and that the spec view carries under each requirement the decisions an agent annotated as informing it, whether or not those decisions are its parents.
:::

:::check{#c-child-placement serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-queries dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8777 DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN=alice bash e2e/acceptance/child-placement.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/child-placement.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: child-placement.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/child-placement.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/child-placement.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Leave the child's part_of to the comment standing when child_of moves it under another parent. The tree read answers the child under the comment of its old parent, and the driver exits non-zero naming the child, the comment and the new parent."}
The driver runs against the `dispatch:local` server of this document's preamble, because it seeds every issue it reads at this head. `e2e/acceptance/child-placement.sh` is new here.

It seeds, as `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN`, one issue with a comment a person wrote, a child issue filed from that comment, a second child with no placement, and a second parent issue outside the first issue's tree.

It places the child issue under the comment that filed it through the re-parent route `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}/parent`, with `{key}` the first issue's key and `{id}` the child issue's store address, percent-encoded as one path segment. It asserts the tree answers the child under that comment. It then moves that placed child under the second parent issue by writing its `child_of`. It reads the child hanging from that new parent issue, with its `part_of` to the comment retracted. The second child, with no placement, hangs from the first issue.
:::

:::check{#c-conversion-scope serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-conversion-scope dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-child-view dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="cli" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN=alice bash e2e/acceptance/conversion-scope.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/conversion-scope.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: conversion-scope.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/conversion-scope.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/conversion-scope.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Four controls, run one at a time. First, let the converter rewrite the `done` issue's spec. Its document digest moves, the driver prints each changed document with its issue key and fails. Second, let the conversation view answer a comment an agent wrote. The driver's read of the child's conversation answers the child's agent comment, prints it and fails, so a child drawn into a discussion thread cannot pass. Third, leave one requirement of the in-flight parent hanging under no exchange. The driver's count of redrawn requirements falls short, it prints that requirement's id, and fails, so a half-redrawn parent cannot pass. Fourth, hold the step in the automatic case: boot this head there with DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS=1 and DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_ISSUE_ROOM_STEP=1. The driver reads converted: false for the in-flight parent after 300 s, and exits non-zero naming that issue."}
The converter touches the issues it must and leaves the rest exactly as they are. The driver seeds four issues through the base-commit server this document's preamble states, because the documents it converts must be ones the earlier release wrote. The first is `done`, with its spec, plan and Verification documents, one ask and one comment thread a person wrote, and no decisions document, because dispatch://INFRA-1150 has converted and deleted every one of those before this child opens, and with the decision nodes INFRA-1150 made of its sections. The second is an in-flight parent with a discussion and three documents. The third is a child of that approved parent, with one comment an agent wrote and no ask. The fourth is a second child of the parent, which holds a requirement node of its own. The driver writes the parent's comments, the done issue's thread and the approval through the base-commit server as `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN`, which that server's dev sign-in admits. It records the byte digest of every document of all four, boots this branch's server, and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states, runs `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`, and reads the digests again after. The `done` issue's spec, plan and Verification documents are byte-identical and its room count is unchanged; any difference is printed with the issue key and the document name and fails the run. The in-flight parent is redrawn, and the driver reads every part of it rather than a sample: its discussion is a graph, every requirement and every verification node of it hangs under an exchange that produced it, its spec view answers those nodes and no prose node, and the count of its requirements before and after is equal. The parent's spec was approved by a person before the conversion. After the redraw it still reads approved, by a carried review at the new version, and every requirement's and every check's words read the same as before. A redraw that changes a requirement's words fails this check. The parent's seeded requirements cite, in their `From:` lines, one ask of the parent, one comment of it, and one ask of an unrelated issue. A fourth requirement cites an unrelated issue's ask first and a comment of the parent second, and hangs under that comment. The `done` issue's `?view=decisions` answers its decision nodes, their readings and their review state, though it did not convert. Its tree read answers `converted: false`, its three document ids, its ask and the thread a person wrote in. After the redraw the first two hang under the ask and the comment they cite, the third hangs from the issue, every author reads as before, and the parent holds no criterion node. A redraw that writes a criterion fails this check. A parent left half redrawn, with one requirement hanging under no exchange, is printed by that count and by the orphan's id, and fails. The child has no conversation tree of its own and carries no approval request of its own. The seeded child raised no ask, so the driver asks for the child's conversation view and reads an empty answer. It then reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks` of the child and finds no ask of kind approval. An ask raised on a child would be in that child's tree, as R23 says and `c-conversation-holds-the-discussion` proves, so the empty answer here is the seed's and not a rule. A planted conversation node under a child, and a planted approval request on a child, are each found by the same two reads, so the absences the check reports are ones its searches could have found.

The second child converts as it stands and is not a view. After the conversion its own requirement node is kept on it, and its spec view answers that requirement as the query's. The driver then proves the automatic case of R6, in a second pass over an emptied `infra_1253_upgrade`. Through the base-commit server it seeds the same four issues, and it keeps that server live. It boots this head beside it without `DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_ISSUE_ROOM_STEP`, and it runs no command. It waits until this head's log holds two lines in which the step names the live process that lists no `issue_room` and converts nothing. It then reads `converted: false` in the tree read of each of the four issues. It stops the base-commit server. It polls every 2 s, and fails after 300 s, until the tree read answers `converted: true` for the in-flight parent and for each child. It reads `converted: false` for the `done` issue, and finds that issue's documents byte-identical to the capture. It finds in this head's log one line for each issue: converted for the parent and for each child, and passed over, with its reason, for the `done` issue.
:::

:::check{#c-child-view serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-child-view dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8777 DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-child-view.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-tree-child-view.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-tree-child-view.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-child-view.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-child-view.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Let the store accept a requirement node on the first child. The driver reads that write accepted where it expects 409, and exits non-zero with a FAIL line naming the child and the requirement it wrote."}
The driver runs against the `dispatch:local` server of this document's preamble, because it reads the head's own store and boots no earlier release. `e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-child-view.sh` is this child's own driver and is new here.

It seeds a parent with two requirement nodes and a first child whose one check serves the first of them. That check hangs from the first child, because it serves no requirement of its own issue. The parent's `?view=verification` answers it through `serves`, marked with the child. It reads the child's Spec view and finds the first requirement and no other, drawn from the parent, and no requirement node on the child.

It writes a requirement node on the first child and reads `409 REQUIREMENT_BELONGS_TO_ANCESTOR` naming the parent. It then reads the child and finds it unchanged.

It reads the parent's coverage and finds the first requirement served by the child's check and the second served by nothing. It records a passed result on the child's check. The parent's verification query then stands at the same version, with the same digest `artifact_version_text_sha256` answers for it, because the parent's record holds no node of the child. It records a passed result on a check of the parent that serves the second, and reads every requirement of the parent covered by a passed check.

It seeds another child under an ancestor that is `done`, writes a requirement node on it, and reads the write accepted.

Each of those reads prints one `PASS:` or `FAIL:` line, and none of them prints `SKIP`, because every section is one this check depends on.
:::

:::check{#c-result-node serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-result-node" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestARecordedResultIsANodeWithItsTuples$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/result-node.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestARecordedResultIsANodeWithItsTuples ' $TMPDIR/result-node.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/result-node.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Write the check_results row and skip the result node. The census in the same test counts one projection row the store does not hold, and the test fails with that result id."}
The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

A result is a node. The test records a result through `recordCheckResult` with two screenshots and reads the node back. The node carries ten values. Those are the verdict, the surface, the run, the observed text, the commit, the role, the three counts and the negative control. The check, the recorder, the session and each screenshot are tuples out of the node, one for each. The result points at the check and at no requirement. The test reads that for a check serving three requirements, and finds one result node under one check.

It reads the `check_results` row written in the same transaction and finds every column equal to the node and its tuples. It rolls that transaction back and finds neither the node, nor a tuple, nor the row. The `check_results` rows an earlier release wrote are read by `c-tree-census`, a driver, because a Go test cannot build an earlier commit.
:::

:::check{#c-shared-id-census serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-move-safe dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-census.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-tree-census.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-tree-census.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-census.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-census.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Seed one issue whose plan-md and whose verification-md each hold a block with id b-r1, take the fresh-id minting out of the merge, and run it. The merged document then holds two nodes under one id, and the driver states that issue, b-r1 and both nodes, and exits non-zero. The same collision with the minting left in is lawful stored data, because document_blocks is keyed (artifact_id, block_id), so the driver reports the count and exits zero; a control that failed on that state would make lawful data a defect."}
The driver publishes, for the whole instance, the count of block ids that stand in more than one document of one issue. It states each issue and each id behind a count above zero. The published count includes the seeded issue and `b-r1`; a count without them fails the run. It takes the count twice and compares the two. It takes it once from the stored rows, keyed as `document_blocks` keys them on `(artifact_id, block_id)`, and once from the blocks the server reads back.

The rows it counts are rows the earlier release wrote, in the pod's test PostgreSQL. They are the corpus the base-commit server seeded, which this document's preamble states: issues carrying a spec, a `verification-md` and a `plan-md`, one of them holding the block id `b-r1` in both its `plan-md` and its `verification-md`. A run whose rows this branch's writer made would prove nothing about the ids already stored. So the driver asserts the source of each row it counted and prints it.

That second read is `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/blocks` for the spec, the Verification document and the plan of the same issue, read after the upgrade and before the conversion, once the backfill the preamble states has run. The two counts must agree exactly, so a count taken from rows a converter has already touched cannot pass for the documents' own. The driver also runs the `.census.sql` this child adds beside the migration that makes block ids unique within an issue, the single `select` the repository runs before a deploy, and reads zero from it. It refuses to report a count it took over no issue.

It then converts that issue with `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE` and reads every block id of the issue's tree once. One `b-r1` keeps its id, the other holds a fresh id, and the old address of each resolves through its `moved_to` tuple.
:::

:::check{#c-redirects serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-move-safe dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-redirects.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-tree-redirects.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-tree-redirects.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-redirects.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-redirects.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Move one node and leave its moved_to tuple out. The dangling_citations line of envoy-dispatch census reads one more than before the move, the citation of that node answers TARGET_NOT_FOUND, and the driver exits non-zero with the old address."}
No citation of a moved node dangles. The citations it tests were written by the earlier release, through the base-commit server this document's preamble states. So the addresses it resolves are addresses that writer stored. The driver writes a comment there that cites a block of the issue's Verification document. Through that server it also writes the five structured pointers at a block of that document: a `refs` row and a `block_refs` row from the citation, an ask with `block_artifact_id` set on that block, a comment whose `anchor` points at the document, and a result on one of its checks, whose `check_results` row holds the `check_artifact_id` and `check_block_id` pair. It plants one prose `#b-` citation of a block no version holds. It records the text each resolver returned and the five pointer columns, `refs.to_id`, `block_refs.to_id`, `asks.block_artifact_id`, `comments.anchor` and that pair, and stops that server. It boots this branch's server and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states. Before the move it reads the five pointer columns as it captured them, so no migration rewrote a pointer. It converts the issue with `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`, which moves that document's blocks into the issue's tree, and reads the citation again. The citation resolves, it reaches the same block at its new address, and the text it returns equals the text captured before the upgrade. Each of the five pointers is a tuple of the store after the move, each projection row equals its tuple, and each points at the node's new home.

It takes that read four ways: the three resolvers R13 names, and `blockReferenceNode` pinned to a version of the old document. Those are the reference read `blockReferenceNode` in `packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/references.go`, the block-link read `refs.BlockLinks` behind `GET /api/v1/block-links`, the issue's reference closure, and the same reference pinned to a version of the old document. It also takes the backlink read `GET /api/v1/references?to=`. The closure takes a target's document out of the node id with `split_part(r.to_id, '#', 1)` in `refs.Closure`'s `documentOfTarget`.

One appended `moved_to` tuple records each pair, the old address and the node, with the time of the move. It runs from the old address to the node, which is the direction dispatch://INFRA-1150 already writes. The driver reads it once and finds no second row for the same move. Before the first move it resolves one citation of a dispatch://INFRA-1150 move through each resolver, which is what dispatch://INFRA-1150 shipped. The dangling-citation counter is the `dangling_citations` line of `envoy-dispatch census`, run against `infra_1253_upgrade`. After the move it reads the same count as before the move, so no citation this move touched dangles. It is not a whole-instance zero: a healthy instance already carries dangling prose `#b-` citations and blocks whose indexing is deferred, which dispatch://INFRA-1150's own check measured, so a whole-instance zero is a gate no correct build could pass. Before the move the line reads 1 or more, counting the planted citation, so a counter that is always zero because it counts nothing fails here. It also proves the order, because the tuples, the resolvers and the counter answer before the first node moves.
:::

:::check{#c-pointers serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-move-safe" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestEveryPointerAtAMovedNodeIsATupleAndItsProjection$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/pointers.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestEveryPointerAtAMovedNodeIsATupleAndItsProjection ' $TMPDIR/pointers.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/pointers.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Leave the check_results pair out of the projection writer. The test reads the recorded result back through its check and fails, because the result belongs to no check node the issue holds."}
The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

On a database that `storetest.Open` migrated to this head, the test writes by SQL, in the shape the release before this one stores, one issue with no `document_rooms` row, whose three documents hold every structured pointer at a block that is about to move. Those are a `refs` row, a `block_refs` row, and an ask with `block_artifact_id` set. They are also a comment whose `anchor` points at the document, and a `check_results` row with its `check_artifact_id` and `check_block_id` pair. `check_results_check` is indexed on that pair.

It writes a `server_build_announcements` row that names the commit the test gives the conversion, so the fleet gate of R6 passes. It converts that issue through the conversion of R6, which moves the nodes, and reads all five back. Each is a tuple of the store, each projection row equals its tuple, and each points at the node's new home. The test rolls the moving transaction back and finds all five as they were.

It then reads the body of a comment and of a message that cite the moved node as prose `#b-` text. The stored bytes are unchanged, character for character, and the citation resolves through the `moved_to` tuple rather than through a rewrite. A pointer at a block that did not move is untouched, row for row.
:::

:::check{#c-approval-bytes serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-approval-bytes dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-serves-coverage dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-approval-hash dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/approval-bytes.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord ' $TMPDIR/approval-bytes.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/approval-bytes.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Two controls, run one at a time. First, build the record from each node's values and body alone, leaving its tuples out. The test retargets one check's serves pointer, reads the digest unchanged, and fails, printing the two targets and the one digest. Second, append the approves tuples and leave the row's approval.documents empty. The test reads the row beside the tuples and fails, naming the ask and the entry the row lacks."}
The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

An approval covers the digest of one query's record, in the tree's own order. The test seeds an issue, approves its spec query, and reads the review. The review pins `content_sha256`, the digest `artifact_version_text_sha256` takes of that version's record. The test builds the record again and gets that digest.

The test pins the relation facts, which is the gap this case exists for. It retargets one check's `serves` pointer from requirement A to requirement B. It changes no word of any node, no value, no identity and no position in the walk. It reads the verification digest and finds it moved. It reads the standing approval of the verification query stale. The broken state this case fails on is a record built from values and body text alone. The digest holds still there while the claimed coverage has changed.

It takes three more relation-only changes the same way. It moves a check under a different requirement, with every word unchanged, and reads the digest moved. It records a result on a check and reads the verification digest moved. `carryVerdict` carries the approval there, and the carried review states the results that arrived after it. It removes a check and reads the digest moved and the approval superseded.

The test pins the order. It reads the record and finds each node before its children, and siblings in increasing rank. It re-ranks two siblings, builds the record again, and reads the two in their new order. It gives two siblings ranks that differ only in case at one position (`a`, `B`) and reads `B` first, because ranks compare byte for byte. The test refuses to run where `select 'a' < 'B'` is false, since such a database cannot tell byte order from its own collation. It writes two siblings holding one rank through the store, builds the record, and reads the lower node id first, comparing ids byte for byte. It writes a value holding the record's own field separators and a value holding a length prefix of its own. It reads two distinct digests, because each field carries its length. It asserts the head record and the record at the approved version run through one builder.

The test pins current approval, not only the historical review. After each change above except the recorded result, which `carryVerdict` carries, it reads the current query's approval state and finds it unapproved. It then reads the issue read's design gate (`issueDesignGatesStatement`, `api/issue_queries.go`) and calls `docs.NamedDocumentsApproved` (`docs/approval_review.go`), and reads each refused, with the query and the digest it compared quoted. It reads the historical review still approved for its own version at the same time. The broken state this case fails on is a build where the old review stays readable, as required. The application there still treats the changed current query as approved.

The test pins what each query takes. The verification query answers the issue's check nodes and the result nodes under them. The spec query answers the memo callout first, where the issue has one, then its criterion and requirement nodes. An edit of one word inside a check node changes the verification digest and leaves the spec approval standing. An edit of a requirement changes the spec digest.

The test pins the move and the column. An approval given before the move still reads approved after it, through the carry Dispatch records in that person's name at the new version, and not through a digest match: a pre-cutover review holds the sha256 of stored markdown, which the length-prefixed record cannot reproduce. The same carry runs for a review whose `content_sha256_source` is `backfill`, so a digest `docs.FillReviewContentHashes` filled at boot decides as one taken at the approval does. A digest comparison applies only to a review taken after the cutover. For such a review the test leaves the query untouched, builds its record again and reads the digest the review already holds. The test reads `artifact_reviews` out of the catalog. It finds `content_sha256` still `text` under the check `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`, with both triggers in place. The migration set runs no statement against that table.

The request's own pointer is a tuple. The test opens an approval request over two queries of one issue. It reads one `approves` tuple per query version node. It reads the `asks` row's `approval.documents` equal to those tuples: one entry for each, holding the artifact uuid and the version integer of that query version node. It reads `asks_approval_kind_check`, `asks_normalize_approval_documents` and its trigger out of the catalog and finds each as the release before left it. It inserts an approval row in the shape the release before writes, and the check admits it. The approval ask's read answers `artifact_id` and `version` equal to the query version node's artifact id and version number, beside `requested_version`. It reads the store revision pinned beside the digest. The answer carry is unchanged. A person's own answer to an ask block still carries as it does today. The test takes that case once before the move and once after, with the same verdict.
:::

:::check{#c-render-at-version serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-render-at-version" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/render-at-version.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples ' $TMPDIR/render-at-version.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/render-at-version.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Read the newest part_of tuple of each node rather than the newest at or before the version's time. The test renders the approved version after a re-parent and fails, because a node comes back under the holder it has now."}
The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

A version the store wrote renders again from the tree. The test writes a subtree, records its rendering and its digest, then re-parents one node, re-orders two siblings and edits the text of a third. It renders the first version again and gets the first bytes, character for character. It renders it twice at different times and gets one byte string both times.

It proves each of the three reads in turn. It takes a node whose text changed and finds the text value of the earlier version. It takes the re-parented node and finds the parent the tuple gives at that time. It takes the re-ordered pair and finds the ranks they held then. It gives two siblings ranks that differ only in case at one position (`a`, `B`) and reads `B` first, because ranks compare byte for byte. The test refuses to run where `select 'a' < 'B'` is false, since such a database cannot tell byte order from its own collation. It retracts a `part_of` tuple after the version's time and renders again, and the node is still in the rendering, because the retraction is later than the version.

It proves the boundary is a row and not a clock. Each version the writer rendered from the tree holds a `version_renders` row, written in the same transaction. The test confirms that by rolling the transaction back and finding neither the version nor the row. It deletes one such row and renders that version again, and the renderer answers the stored markdown and says so. It appends a tuple dated before a pre-cutover version and renders that version. The answer is unchanged, because no tuple moves a version across the boundary. It reads the digest of a pre-cutover version and finds it taken over that version's stored markdown. It reads the digest of a post-cutover version and finds it taken over that version's record.

It reads the head rendering through the same renderer with the time set to now and finds the current tree. It compares `document_block_texts` with the appended text values over a converted issue and finds zero differences in both directions. It writes by SQL, in the shape the release before this one stores, `document_block_texts` rows of a document whose issue has no `document_rooms` row. The census prints those rows as the class of issues that have not converted, with their count, and counts none of them as a difference. It reads the catalog and finds the table's columns as `packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/migrations/0121_block_graph.up.sql` creates them.
:::

:::check{#c-old-versions-render serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-render-at-version dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-approval-bytes dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-approval-hash" surface="cli" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN=alice bash e2e/acceptance/version-render-boundary.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/version-render-boundary.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: version-render-boundary.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/version-render-boundary.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/version-render-boundary.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Render one pre-cutover version from the tuples instead of returning its stored bytes. The driver compares that render with artifact_versions.markdown, finds them unequal, and exits non-zero with the artifact, the version number and the first byte that differs."}
Every version written before the cutover still answers the bytes it holds, and every standing approval still covers them. The driver runs against the pod's test PostgreSQL, over a corpus the earlier release wrote. It builds and boots the base-commit server as this document's preamble states. Through that server's API it writes markdown documents of the shapes `c-tree-census` lists, with several versions each, and one image upload, whose version holds no markdown. It also writes one document holding a block written author-only. It records an approval of the newest version of some of those documents, so the corpus holds standing approvals, and it stops that server. It then boots this branch's server, which migrates those rows forward, and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states, and from then on it writes nothing. It first prints the two counts this child's first step took over that corpus. Those are the count of `artifact_versions` rows with a markdown body and the count of standing approvals, each with the time it was taken. A count of zero fails the run, because the corpus holds both.

It then renders every version row with a markdown body, and prints how many it rendered. For each version it calls the one renderer and compares the answer with `artifact_versions.markdown`, byte for byte. That comparison is made as a reader who may see every block of the version. A version stored before this child's cutover can still hold a block written author-only, because dispatch://INFRA-1950 lands first. So the driver also renders such a version as a reader the block is hidden from, and reads that block absent, with the rest of the version byte for byte as stored. The run fails unless at least one rendered version holds a block written author-only. Every version must match. One mismatch fails the run, and the driver prints the artifact, the version number and the offset of the first byte that differs. It also asserts that no rendered version holds a `version_renders` row, so the set is the pre-cutover side and not the new one.

It then takes the approvals. For each standing approval over a rendered version it recomputes the digest `artifact_version_text_sha256` takes of the stored markdown and compares it with `artifact_reviews.content_sha256`. Every one must be equal, and one difference fails the run. That comparison tests that the stored bytes did not change, and it is not a test of an approval digest, because a review taken before the cutover is carried rather than digested again, as R14 states. It reads the update trigger on that column out of the catalog and finds it in place. Last it reads a version whose `markdown` is null and finds the renderer saying it holds no bytes, rather than answering an empty document.
:::

:::check{#c-tuple-indexes serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-tuple-indexes" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestEveryAsOfReadOfThisChildUsesAnIndexOfTheStore$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/tuple-indexes.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestEveryAsOfReadOfThisChildUsesAnIndexOfTheStore ' $TMPDIR/tuple-indexes.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/tuple-indexes.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Write the as-of render's read without its kind predicate. The test reads a Seq Scan on graph_tuples in that read's plan and fails, naming the read."}
The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

Every read this child makes is served by an index child one created. The test reads the five read index definitions out of the catalog and compares them with the five spellings the spec states, column for column, order for order and predicate for predicate. A missing index fails the test and prints which read it served.

It then takes the plan of each read. Those reads are the as-of read of a node's text, parent and rank, and the children of a node in rank order at a time. They are also the `moved_to` resolve, the `needs` walk in both directions, the coverage walk over `serves`, and the backlink count. It seeds 50,000 tuples over 500 nodes and runs `analyze graph_tuples`. For each read it runs `explain (analyze, buffers)`, and asserts that the plan uses the stated index as an `Index Scan`, `Index Only Scan` or `Bitmap Index Scan`, with no `Seq Scan on graph_tuples` anywhere in it. A read that binds no kind is written into the test as a case that must fail. The test reads that case falling to a scan. Among the seeded siblings, two have ranks that differ only in case at one position (`a`, `B`), and the children read returns `B` first, because ranks compare byte for byte. The test refuses to run where `select 'a' < 'B'` is false, since such a database cannot tell byte order from its own collation.

Last it reads the migration set of this child with `pgmigrate.TouchedTables`. It finds no statement against the tuple table outside the type migrations that `typeMigrations` lists in `packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/supertag_nodes_test.go`, and only `insert` statements in those.
:::

:::check{#c-artifacts-in-tree serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-artifacts-in-tree dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/issue-artifacts.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-artifacts.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-artifacts.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-artifacts.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-artifacts.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Leave one uploaded image out of the tree, as a row with no node. The driver walks the issue's tree, counts one artifact the walk does not reach, and exits non-zero with that artifact's ref key."}
Every artifact of an issue is in the tree. The driver uploads a markdown document, an image and a file to one issue, and walks the issue's tree. It reaches all three as nodes under the issue. It reads the image node and finds its mime, its size and its sha256 as values of the node. It reads the image's bytes back through `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug}/versions/{number}`, byte for byte.

It repeats the whole walk over an issue the earlier release wrote. It builds and boots the base-commit server as this document's preamble states. It uploads the same three artifacts through that server's API, records each artifact's ref key, bytes and version count, and stops it. It boots this branch's server, which migrates those rows forward, and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states, and walks that issue's tree. Every artifact that writer stored is a node, and each one's bytes and version count equal the capture. The broken state this ordering catches is a migration that reaches every artifact its own writer made. Such a migration can still miss one shape the earlier release stored.

It reads the markdown document and finds its body as a subtree of block nodes, rendered by one query. It writes a new version and reads the document version node appended for it, with the rendering stored in `artifact_versions.markdown` as the cache. It compares that stored markdown against a fresh render of the tree at that version's time and finds them equal. It takes that comparison over the versions `version_renders` holds, and asserts the census claims nothing about a version with no such row.

It then reads the three role documents of an issue the earlier release wrote, converted with `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`. Their blocks hang under the issue, and each of the three reads back as a query node that states the node types it takes. In the answers of `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts` and `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug}`, the `role` of each query node is the name of its query. No column of the converted issue's `artifacts` rows holds a role. It reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}` and finds `verification_artifact_id` and `plan_artifact_id` still answered, each with the artifact id of its query node, as R8 keeps them for one release. It runs the role census R16 states, which counts the `artifacts` rows that carry a role on issues whose documents have `document_rooms` rows, and reads 0. A role planted on one row of the converted issue is counted by the same census. No migration of this branch drops `artifacts.role`.
:::

:::check{#c-search-key serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-search-key" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^(TestSearchFollowsABlockThatChangesOwner|TestThisBuildBootsRemovesAndErasesWithTheRootsSearchTablesDropped)$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/search-key.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestSearchFollowsABlockThatChangesOwner ' $TMPDIR/search-key.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestThisBuildBootsRemovesAndErasesWithTheRootsSearchTablesDropped ' $TMPDIR/search-key.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/search-key.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Four controls, run one at a time. The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

A block that changes owner changes the key search uses. The test indexes a document's blocks, reads the window rows under the artifact uuid as owner key, then moves the blocks into the issue's tree. It reads the windows again under the issue's tree node as owner key and finds every block covered once. It finds the old owner's rows still stored, and the census counts them as the class the root deletes. It searches by meaning for the moved block's words through this build and reads the block once.

It rolls back the transaction that writes the block rows and finds the old owner's windows still present and none under the issue's tree node. It commits it and finds the windows under the issue's tree node, with the old owner's windows still stored. It reads `embeddings_kind_check` out of the catalog and finds it unchanged, and asserts the migration set runs no statement against `embeddings`.

It then holds the lexical search. It writes a word into one block, and reads `node_search` holding that word for that node. It reads the search route answering the node that matched rather than a document. It reads the catalog and finds the `artifact_versions_document_search` trigger, its function and the `document_search` table still in place, because a process of the release before reads that table and only that trigger fills it. It writes a version and reads the `document_search` row that trigger filled. It then empties `document_search` and reads the same answer from the search route, so this build's search reads `node_search` alone. It reads the migration set with `pgmigrate.TouchedTables` and finds no statement against `artifact_versions` or `document_search`. A second test, `TestThisBuildBootsRemovesAndErasesWithTheRootsSearchTablesDropped` in `packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch`, builds this head with `cmdtest.Build`, migrates a database of its own, and drops there what the root's pull request drops: `document_search` with the `artifact_versions_document_search` trigger and its function, `document_search_term_queue()` with its trigger, and `document_search_backfill`. It boots this head over that database, reads `/healthz` answer 200, then removes one document and erases a graph node, and reads both succeed, because each statement of this build that names `document_search` runs only where `to_regclass('public.document_search')` finds the table. Before the drop, the test lets the block drain finish and removes the document whose id `issue_tree_block_drain`'s cursor holds; it reads that table still holding its one row with `done` true, and the boot reads `/healthz` 200, so no removal deletes the drain's record, the defect dispatch://INFRA-4018 fixes for `document_search_backfill`. The run greps its log for the `--- PASS:` line of each test by itself.
