:::check{#c-one-dependency serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-one-dependency dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-plan-size dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-needs dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-plan-node dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-issue-edges" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/one-dependency.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/one-dependency.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: one-dependency.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/one-dependency.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/one-dependency.log &amp;&amp; cd ../envoy &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestNeedsCrossesAProjectAndRefusesAProjectScopedCaller$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/needs-reach.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestNeedsCrossesAProjectAndRefusesAProjectScopedCaller ' $TMPDIR/needs-reach.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/needs-reach.log &amp;&amp; cd ../daemon &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestTheDaemonReadsNeedsAndFallsBackToBlockedBy$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/daemon-needs.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheDaemonReadsNeedsAndFallsBackToBlockedBy ' $TMPDIR/daemon-needs.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/daemon-needs.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Three controls, run one at a time. First, keep the issue route writing issue_links rows as the record and leave the plan pointer on its own kind. The driver reads one needs tuple for the plan dependency and none for the issue dependency, and exits non-zero with both reads side by side. Second, refuse a needs target of another project to a caller that names no project. The driver reads that refusal where it expects the wait taken, and exits non-zero naming the two issues and their projects. Third, name the issue wait needs in this child's restatement of graph_edges. The driver reads no blocked_by edge in graph_edges for the issue dependency, and exits non-zero naming the two issues and the kind it read."}
Waiting is one relation and the driver proves both halves answer as one. It seeds a parent issue whose plan holds two nodes, and a child issue whose plan holds two more. It writes an issue dependency through the issue route, from the child issue to a sibling issue of the same project. It writes a plan dependency in markdown, from one of the child's nodes to a node of the parent's plan.

It reads both back as `needs` tuples of the store, each from the node that waits to the node it waits on. It reads `issue_links` holding the issue pair as a row, and reads the `needs` attribute of the plan node holding its target in markdown. So both are projections of one relation. It reads `graph_edges` naming the issue wait `blocked_by`, as a process of the release before reads it, and the plan wait `needs`. It reads `GET /api/v1/references?from=<issue ref>` answering the issue wait as `needs`. It reads that same edge through `?kind=needs` and through `?kind=blocked_by`, because the kind filter takes both spellings. It retracts the issue dependency through the issue route and, on its next read with no pass run, finds the `issue_links` row gone. It writes one dependency through `dispatch issue-update --blocked-by`, which sends `needs` and `blocked_by` with the same targets, and reads the one `needs` tuple it appended. It also reads one `issue_links` row the earlier release wrote, captured as this document's preamble states, answering as a `needs` tuple after the upgrade, once the backfill the preamble states has run.

It reads the reach and the refusals each writer keeps. It creates a second project, `CORE2`, through `POST /api/v1/projects`, with `default_assignee` set to `alice`. It writes a `needs` from an issue of `CORE` to an issue of `CORE2` through the agent bearer, which names no project, and the write is taken. The Go test `TestNeedsCrossesAProjectAndRefusesAProjectScopedCaller` in `internal/dispatch/api` writes the same wait with a credential that names one project, and reads `403 PROJECT_SCOPE`, for `needs` as for `blocked_by`. A target set above `contracts.MaxIssueBlockers` is refused `400 NEEDS_INPUT` when the request names `needs`, and `400 BLOCKED_BY_INPUT` when it names `blocked_by`. A request that names `needs` and `blocked_by` with the same targets appends one `needs` tuple for each target, and one whose two lists differ is refused with status 400, and the error names both. An issue that would wait on itself through the relation and the parent chain is refused `409 DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`. A plan node pointing at a plan node of an issue outside its own tree is refused, which `refs.IssueAncestors` decides. The cross-issue `needs` from the child's plan node to the parent's is taken, which `pmdoc.CheckBlockPointers` refuses today for `scope: "document"`. It also writes, in a second document of the child issue, a plan task whose `needs` names a task of the child's own plan. `e2e/acceptance/verification.sh` asserts today that this cross-document `needs` within one issue is refused, because `pmdoc.CheckBlockPointers` holds `needs` to its own document. This child takes it, because both ends are plan nodes of one issue, and the driver reads its `needs` tuple. This work replaces that assertion of `verification.sh` with the refusal of a `needs` that names a plan task of an issue outside the writer's tree.

The Go test `TestTheDaemonReadsNeedsAndFallsBackToBlockedBy` in `packages/daemon/internal/dispatch` decodes an issue answer that holds `needs` and one that holds `blocked_by` alone, and finds the same targets in both. Last it reads the sizes. Three of the four plan nodes carry one. The driver reads each back character for character as its author wrote it, through the node's attributes and through `dispatch read --ref`. It reads no size at all on the fourth, absent rather than present and empty. A size the schema does not allow is refused `400 INVALID_MARKDOWN`, the shape `verification.sh` already asserts for a `when` the schema does not know.
:::

:::check{#c-view-arms serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-issue-relations dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-no-regression" surface="cli" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE PRE_1149_SHA=${PRE_1149_SHA:-$(git merge-base origin/main origin/legion/INFRA-1149)} bash e2e/acceptance/view-arms-rollback.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/view-arms-rollback.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: view-arms-rollback.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/view-arms-rollback.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/view-arms-rollback.log &amp;&amp; cd ../envoy &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback ' $TMPDIR/TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Three controls, run one at a time. First, delete the `blocked_by` arm in this child's migration: the link the release before writes with no node is missing from the view and from the outbound references read GET /api/v1/references?from=&lt;issue ref&gt;, and the test fails naming it. Second, make the deletion of dispatch://INFRA-1149's four arms skip its guard: over the database the driver migrates from the release before dispatch://INFRA-1149, the four go at this child's first boot, and the driver fails naming them. Third, drop the `offset 0` from the probe of `issue_links` in this child's restatement of `graph_edges`: the plan of a `graph_edges` read of one issue holds a Seq Scan on issue_links, and the test fails naming that table."}
The test reads `pg_get_viewdef('graph_edges', true)` at this child's head and splits it on the top-level `union all`. The four arms dispatch://INFRA-1149 moved are gone, and so is the tuple arm's join for their kinds. The `child_of` and `blocked_by` arms, the three component arms and the `artifact attached_to issue` arm stand, each answering only the rows with no `node_kind`, and the tuple arm answers their kinds only while the projection row that names the edge carries its node. The arm over `refs` stands too, and it answers a row from an artifact only while that artifact carries no node. It seeds, by SQL, a database as the release before this one leaves it: a stamped issue link, a link that release wrote with no node, and a stamped link that release deleted with no retraction, and the same three for a parent, a component's parent and a component dependency. It reads `graph_edges`, `refs.BacklinkCounts` and the outbound references read `GET /api/v1/references?from=<issue ref>`, which `Links:` of `dispatch read --issue` renders, and finds each standing relation once, and each deleted one nowhere. In `graph_edges` each stands under the name a process of the release before reads, so an issue link is `blocked_by` in the old arm and in the tuple arm. The references read answers that link as `needs`. It seeds an issue link, a parent, a component's parent, a component dependency, an artifact on an issue and a document's citation of another issue, each written before this child, with no node. Before this child's backfill each is answered once, by its old arm. After it each is answered once, by the tuple arm, dated with its row's own `created_at`, and the old arms answer none of them. It then runs this child's deletion of the four old arms over a database where a block row is deleted by SQL, as a build of the release before dispatch://INFRA-1149 deletes it, and its tuple stands: the four arms stay, the server starts and serves, and its log names the difference. Over a database with no difference, whose newest announcement naming another build lists the four arms' kinds, the four are gone. The driver `e2e/acceptance/view-arms-rollback.sh`, new here, proves the half that needs an earlier build. It reads the input `PRE_1149_SHA`, the release before dispatch://INFRA-1149, which the run defaults to `git merge-base origin/main origin/legion/INFRA-1149`. Once that branch merges, the implementer sets it to the first parent of its merge commit on `main`, and the handoff names the value. The driver calls `lib-baseline.sh`'s `baseline_start` with `BASELINE_SHA` set to `PRE_1149_SHA`. Through that server's API it writes an issue link, a parent, a component's parent and a component dependency, and it stops that server. It inserts by SQL an announcement of that release that names `PRE_1149_SHA`, because `lib-baseline.sh` builds with no stamped commit. It boots this branch's server over the same database and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states. The four arms stay, and every edge reads as before through `graph_edges`, the issue link under `blocked_by`. `GET /api/v1/references?from=<issue ref>` answers each edge once, the issue link as `needs`. The same holds through a second process of this build, started beside the first, and again after a restart of it. Once an announcement of a build listing those kinds is recorded, the first boot of a later build deletes them. Over a database this boot created from empty, the four are gone at once. The test seeds 50,000 issue links, parents and component rows over 500 issues, runs `analyze`, and takes `explain (analyze, buffers)` of a `graph_edges` read of one issue. It finds no `Seq Scan` of `issues`, `issue_links`, `components`, `component_depends` or `issue_component_members` in that plan. The run proves the test executed, because the command reads `--- PASS: TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback` out of the kept output and fails on any `--- SKIP` line. It reads the driver's `PASS: view-arms-rollback.sh complete` line the same way, and fails on any `SKIP` line of the driver.
:::

:::check{#c-role-kind serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-artifacts-in-tree dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-no-regression" surface="api" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./internal/dispatch/api/... -run '^TestAFileNamedLikeARoleDocumentPlaysNoRole$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/TestAFileNamedLikeARoleDocumentPlaysNoRole.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAFileNamedLikeARoleDocumentPlaysNoRole ' $TMPDIR/TestAFileNamedLikeARoleDocumentPlaysNoRole.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/TestAFileNamedLikeARoleDocumentPlaysNoRole.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Two controls, run one at a time. First, take the kind test out of documentRolePredicate. The tree read of the first unconverted issue answers the upload's id as its plan document, and the test fails naming that id and its slug. Second, let the plan query take a node by its document's slug. The upload's node appears in ?view=plan of the converted issue, and the test fails naming it."}
The test proves two cases. On an issue that has not converted, a role-less upload named `plan.md` whose bytes are not markdown plays no role. The test creates that issue through this head's writers. It writes by SQL, in the shape the release before this one stores, the issue's spec of kind `doc`, and the upload as kind `file` with slug `plan-md` and no role, as `20261102110000_artifact_document_roles.up.sql` allows, with no `document_rooms` row. It reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree`, finds `converted: false`, and finds no plan document id in the answer, so the upload does not play the plan. It writes a second such issue whose role-less row of kind `doc` has the slug `plan-md`, which is the row a rolling deploy leaves, and reads that row's id as the plan document. On an issue born converted, an upload named `plan.md` whose bytes are not markdown is a `file` node under the issue, `?view=plan` answers no node of it, and the issue's plan query node and its version count are unchanged. The same holds for an upload named `verification.md`: it is a `file` node under the issue, `?view=verification` answers no node of it, and the issue's verification query node and its version count are unchanged. The run proves the test executed, because the command reads `--- PASS: TestAFileNamedLikeARoleDocumentPlaysNoRole` out of the kept output and fails on any `--- SKIP` line.
:::

:::check{#c-ordered-read serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-ordered-read dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-needs dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-plan-node" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestTheOrderedReadWalksTheWholeTreeAndReportsEveryCycle$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/ordered-read.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheOrderedReadWalksTheWholeTreeAndReportsEveryCycle ' $TMPDIR/ordered-read.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/ordered-read.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Walk the plan nodes of one issue alone, as the read did before. The test seeds a cycle that runs from a child issue through a plan node of its parent and back, and fails, because the read answers an order and reports no cycle."}
The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

One read answers the order the whole tree runs in. The test seeds a parent issue and two child issues, each with plan nodes, and writes `needs` tuples of both kinds across them. It reads one answer holding every issue and every plan node of that tree. Each node stands once, after every node it needs, with its size beside it.

It proves the two halves. An issue is placed as a start and a done, as `waitNode` splits it. A parent issue holding a child is no cycle, and the parent's done sits after every child's done. A plan node's start sits after its issue's start, and its issue's done sits after that plan node. A sibling issue waiting on another sibling keeps its order.

The test then seeds cycles. Two plan nodes of one issue need each other. A longer cycle of three crosses two issues of one tree, which the widened reach now lets a writer make. A third runs from an issue to a plan node of another issue and back. The read reports each cycle with the nodes in it and returns no order that hides one. A node that needs itself is a cycle of one and is reported. Every node outside a cycle keeps its position, so one bad plan does not blank the answer. A plan with no cycle reports none, including a diamond where two nodes need a third and a fourth needs both, so the detector does not cry wolf. A parent's plan node that needs its child issue comes back after every plan node of that child and after the child's done half. A child's plan node that needs that same parent plan node makes a cycle, which the read reports with the parent plan node, the child's done half and the child's plan node in it. A plan node that needs an issue outside its own issue's tree is refused at the write. The control: let the read take the child's start half for a `needs` on an issue, and the parent's plan node comes back before the child's plan nodes, which the test names.
:::

:::check{#c-migration-size serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-migration-size" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestThisChildsMigrationsTouchNoTableAboveTheCensusLimit$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/migration-size.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestThisChildsMigrationsTouchNoTableAboveTheCensusLimit ' $TMPDIR/migration-size.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/migration-size.log &amp;&amp; gh pr view legion/INFRA-1253 --repo cybermonklabs/legion --json body --jq .body &gt; $TMPDIR/pr-body.md &amp;&amp; cd ../dispatch &amp;&amp; bash e2e/acceptance/migration-census-body.sh $TMPDIR/migration-size.log $TMPDIR/pr-body.md 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/migration-census-body.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: migration-census-body.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/migration-census-body.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/migration-census-body.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Add a migration that drops the artifact_versions_document_search trigger. The test reads artifact_versions among the tables that migration touches and fails, naming the migration and the statement."}
The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

No migration of this child touches a table above the limit except through an exempt statement kind. The test reads every migration this child adds and runs `pgmigrate.TouchedTables` over each. For each table a migration touches it runs the census with a table limit of one byte, as `packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/census_test.go` sets one, and reads the verdict. Two tables take a second run: a type migration appends its supertag and attribute rows to `graph_nodes` and `graph_tuples` with `insert`, which no limit of one byte admits. For those two tables the test runs the census at `pgmigrate.CensusTableLimit` and prints one `SIZE: <table> <bytes the census read> <the limit>` line for each. On `graph_tuples` a type migration's statements are `insert` alone. On `graph_nodes` they are `insert`, and an `update` whose `where` names `kind = 'supertag'` or `kind = 'attribute'`, which is how the type migration `20261113230000_graph_supertags_check_ci_check` on `main` moves the schema version that a server installs from a type node's attributes. The test fails on any other statement on either table: an `update` of another kind of node, a `delete`, an `alter table` or a `truncate`.

No migration of this child touches `artifact_versions` at all. The test fails on a `drop trigger` or a `drop function` of `artifact_versions_document_search`, and on any other statement that names that table. It fails the same way on a statement that names `document_search`, `asks_approval_kind_check` or `asks_normalize_approval_documents`, because all of them stay. It asserts that no migration of this child touches `doc_updates`, `doc_snapshots`, `doc_checkpoints`, `document_block_texts`, `embeddings`, `check_results`, `artifact_versions`, `artifact_reviews` or `document_blocks` in an `alter table`, a `drop table` or a `truncate`. It asserts that the only statement on `issue_links` is the `add column` of the nullable node column pair with no default, which `catalogOnlyAlterTable` exempts, and it fails on any other `alter table`, on a `drop table` and on a `truncate` of that table. It reads the two tables this child creates, `document_rooms` and `version_renders`, and finds each created new and read by no backfill of a stored row.

The test prints one `TOUCHED: <table>` line for each table the migration set touches, and one `SHAPE: <table>` line for each table whose shape a migration changes. It reads no pull request, so it runs on `main` with no token. The run's last step reads the pull request body once, at the head the implementer hands off, with `gh pr view`. `e2e/acceptance/migration-census-body.sh`, new here, reads that body beside the test's log. It prints the sizing projection that the body records for each table beside the `SIZE:` line of that table, so a reader sees how far each of the two tables stands below the limit. It finds every `TOUCHED:` table listed, each with the recorded reading of its size and that reading's source where one stands. It finds the two counts of the render boundary beside them, of the versions written before the cutover and of the standing approvals, taken over the seeded corpus of `c-old-versions-render`. A table missing from that list fails the script, which prints the table. So does a recorded reading at or above `pgmigrate.CensusTableLimit` for a `SHAPE:` table, with no raise of that constant in `internal/pgmigrate/census.go` beside it in the same branch, and so does a count of zero.
:::

:::check{#c-order serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-order dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-room-cutover" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-order.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-tree-order.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-tree-order.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-order.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-order.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Two controls, run one at a time. First, convert the spec before verification-md inside the conversion transaction. The seq of the spec's first part_of is lower than verification-md's, and the driver exits non-zero printing the three seqs in the order it read them. Second, delete the route GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions in this branch. The driver finds that route of BASELINE_SHA missing at this head, and exits non-zero naming it."}
The driver proves the order. The issue it converts was written by the earlier release, through the base-commit server this document's preamble states. The driver captured its three documents before the upgrade. It boots this branch's server, waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states, converts that issue with `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`, and reads the three documents converted inside one transaction. Within that transaction, the `graph_tuples.seq` of the first `part_of` written for each document's nodes rises in the order `verification-md`, `plan-md`, spec. It reads the issue's census at zero after that transaction. It finds no issue in `infra_1253_upgrade` left with some documents converted and some not.

It reads the query nodes and the approval rule answering before the first node moves. It reads `version_renders` and the render boundary answering before the first node moves too. It reads the block schema the server serves and finds the version after dispatch://INFRA-1150's, since that child lands before this one and two children cannot share one version: an editor cached at INFRA-1150's version would stay writable and drop the criterion it cannot see. That version carries the criterion type, the requirement's `serves` attribute, the `size` attribute, the widened `needs` scope and the `items` field. The node `state` values `proposed`, `settled` and `overtaken` ride no block schema bump, because the node `state` is a store attribute of a graph node, not a block attribute. A second bump anywhere in the branch fails the run.

It then reads `git log --reverse --format=%H origin/main..HEAD`. With `git log -S` for each of `requirementBlocksIn` and `checkBlocksIn`, the document lookups that only this build runs, it finds the commit that deletes the name later in that list than the commit that adds the route `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree` to `packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/routes_table.go`. No route goes: it reads the routes of that file at `BASELINE_SHA` and at this head, and finds every route of the first in the second, `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` among them. It reads one dependency through `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}`, `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/summary` and `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/events`, and finds `blocked_by` beside `needs` in each, as R10 keeps it through this child. Both answer from the `needs` tuples, and the stored `issue_links` row is their projection. A PATCH that names `needs` and `blocked_by` with the same targets is served from them, and one whose two lists differ is refused with status 400, and the error names both. It finds no route and no field of the issue read that answers null for ever.
:::

:::check{#c-tree-page serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-queries dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-one-tree dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-one-room dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="cli" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-spec-query.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-tree-spec-query.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-tree-spec-query.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-spec-query.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-spec-query.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Answer the tree read's nodes in node id order rather than in the walk order. Two siblings come back out of rank order, and the driver exits non-zero naming their parent and the two siblings in the order it read them."}
The driver builds and boots the base-commit server as this document's preamble states. Through its API it writes one issue with no parent that is not `done`. It holds a spec of two requirement blocks and a Verification document of two check blocks that serve them. It holds a plan of one plan node that serves one of those requirements. The driver records each block's id, text and `serves` targets, and stops that server. It boots this branch's server over the same database and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states.

With every live process and the newest announcement at the conversion's own stamped commit, the driver runs `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`. So the driver converts rows the earlier release stored.

The driver reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree` once. The answer reads `converted: true`. It holds each requirement, each check and the plan node as one node. Each node carries its id, its supertag, its parent and its rank. Each node's parent is the issue's node or another node of the answer. Each parent stands before its children, and siblings stand in increasing rank, compared byte for byte. The driver refuses to run, printing a FAIL line, where `select 'a' < 'B'` is false, since such a database cannot tell byte order from its own collation.

The same answer holds every `serves` tuple among those nodes. The driver walks the `serves` tuples from each requirement. It reaches each check whose `serves` names that requirement, and the plan node whose `serves` names it. The set it reaches equals the set the earlier release wrote. A second read answers the same nodes in the same order.

The driver reads `?view=spec` from the same route. That answer holds the two requirement nodes, each marked as the query's, in the order the first read gave them. Each carries its parent's id, supertag and first line. The driver reads the issue read, `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}`, and finds the spec query node. That node states the node types it takes, which are the types R14 gives the spec query. It states the subtree it takes them from, which starts at the issue's tree node.

The driver changes one word of a check and one word of the plan node in one write of the issue's room. The two nodes stood in the Verification document and in the plan before the conversion. The driver reads the tree and finds both new words.

`e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-spec-query.sh` is this check's own driver and is new here.
:::
